issues.detail: Error handling is mostly limited to fallbacks; it gives no guidance on rate limits, timeouts, auth failures, streaming errors, or database misconfiguration for virtual keys, and no troubleshooting steps.
The two examples are prose descriptions that point back to earlier snippets instead of showing full runnable input and output, so they are simplistic.

The skill recommends pinning versions, verifying images and using a venv, which are good supply-chain practices; the only items worth noting are that the docker tag `main-stable` is a floating tag and the skill itself says to verify it.

scenarios.name: claude-to-gpt-fallback-router
scenarios.rationale: Response B builds the required litellm Router with anthropic/ and openai/ deployments, env-var keys, fallbacks=[{"smart": ["fast"]}], num_retries=2, and reads r.choices[0].message.content, while Response A hand-rolls the logic with the raw SDKs and never uses litellm.

scenarios.name: team-proxy-virtual-keys-budget
scenarios.rationale: Both give a valid LiteLLM config with os.environ/ refs, master_key and database_url, and a /key/generate call with max_budget 25, rpm_limit and user_id; B states that the master key must start with sk- and that the database is PostgreSQL, and it has an explicit /key/info spend-check command with the master key header, while A mentions /key/info only in passing in the notes without a command and its master_key and database_url are env references without those comments (though its .env sets sk-master- and compose uses Postgres).

scenarios.name: safe-install-pinned-litellm
scenarios.rationale: B states the March 2026 malicious 1.82.7/1.82.8 releases as fact, pins an exact version, uses openai/ and gemini/ prefixes, reads r.choices[0].message.content, and mentions a lock file. A hedges on the incident, leaves the version as a placeholder, uses an unprefixed gpt-4o-mini, and never mentions a lock file.
